title: Renal transplant under Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme successful
summary: Surgeons at Meenkashi Hospital in Thanjavur successfully performed a live-related renal transplant in March 2025 under the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme. The patient, diagnosed with chronic kidney disease in 2019 and on haemodialysis, received a kidney from his wife and is recovering without signs of rejection. Nephrologist S. Gowri Shankar urged families to consider organ donation given donor shortages.
content:
Published- April 18, 2025 06:59 pm IST - THANJAVUR

A surgical procedure of transplanting a kidney carried out under the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister’s Health Insurance Scheme at Meenkashi Hospital, Thanjavur, was successful with the patient responding well after the procedure.

According to S. Gowri Shankar, Consultant – Nephrology, the patient was diagnosed with chronic kidney disease in 2019, though the exact cause was not known. With his condition worsening, the risk of high morbidity and mortality was significant. He underwent haemodialysis for months. And a live-related renal allograft transplant was performed in March 2025.

The procedure was complex, but it was smooth, Dr. Gowri Shankar added and said that both the patient and the donor were recovering well, with no sign of organ rejection. The patient was fortunate to find a matching donor in his wife, Dr. Gowri Shankar said and added that there was shortage of donors and hence urged families of such patients to come forward and consider donating kidneys of their deceased kin.
